description: Minimal process overhead recommended for solo developers

action.recommendation: Solo projects benefit from lightweight processes. Focus on a clear README, basic git hygiene (meaningful commits), and simple CI. Avoid ceremony that adds friction without value for a team of one.

rationale: Heavy processes designed for teams add friction without benefit for solo developers.

description: Code review process recommended for pair/trio teams

action.recommendation: Establish a lightweight code review process for your pair/trio team. Use PRs or merge requests for all significant changes. Define what requires review, set a response time SLA (e.g. 24 hours), and document the review checklist.

rationale: Even small teams benefit from code review to share knowledge, catch bugs, and maintain consistency.

description: CODEOWNERS file required for small teams

action.recommendation: Create a CODEOWNERS file to define code ownership for your small team. Assign owners for critical paths (auth, payments, core APIs). This ensures the right reviewer is automatically requested for sensitive changes.

rationale: Without explicit ownership, critical changes go unreviewed by subject matter experts in growing teams.

description: Architecture overview document recommended for small teams

action.recommendation: Create a lightweight architecture overview document for your small team. Document system components, data flows, key technology decisions, and integration points. Update when making significant architectural changes.

rationale: Small teams grow. Architecture documentation prevents knowledge concentration in individuals and supports onboarding.

description: Cross-team governance required for multi-team organisations

action.recommendation: Establish cross-team governance structures. Define an Architecture Review Board (ARB) or RFC process for significant changes, create an API versioning policy, establish shared coding standards, and document team boundaries and ownership.

rationale: Multiple teams without governance produce incompatible APIs, conflicting standards, and integration failures.

description: Shared library strategy required for multi-team organisations

action.recommendation: Define a shared library strategy for common utilities. Document what belongs in shared libraries vs team-owned code, establish library versioning and deprecation policies, set up an internal package registry, and assign library maintainers.

rationale: Without a shared library strategy, multi-team organisations duplicate code and accumulate inconsistent implementations.

description: Designate compliance officer for enterprise organisations

action.recommendation: Designate a Compliance Officer or DPO for your enterprise organisation. Document their responsibilities, ensure they have authority to enforce policies, and integrate compliance review into the SDLC. Maintain a compliance register.

rationale: Enterprise organisations face complex regulatory requirements that require dedicated compliance oversight.

description: Formal API versioning policy required for enterprise

action.recommendation: Implement a formal API versioning policy for enterprise APIs. Use semantic versioning, define deprecation timelines (minimum 12 months), publish API changelogs, provide migration guides, and enforce versioning via API gateway policies.

rationale: Enterprise APIs serve many internal and external consumers. Breaking changes without versioning cause widespread integration failures.
